lead: >-

  Iguazu Falls, continues amid the dry landscapes of the Atacama and leads to
  the high-altitude roads of the Andes and Machu Picchu. However, the longest
  off-road section of the relevant itineraries lies in Bolivia, which they
  include as a fifth principal country. Compare walking days, flights and 4×4
  journeys to choose according to actual demands, not just the theme's name.

## What an adventure tour through four countries really means

**The "Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Peru: Adventure" selection brings together long itineraries that visit these four countries on the same trip.** The relevant programmes also pass through Bolivia. They are therefore not a collection of standalone ready-made tours restricted to four countries: the adventure element is largely shaped by the Bolivian crossing in 4×4 vehicles.

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. All combine city excursions, walks in nature, flights and high-altitude transfers. The intensity varies between days: alongside demanding sections at Iguazu and in the Andes, there are calmer days in Rio, Buenos Aires and Lima. To compare programmes without the theme filter, see the [general Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Peru catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile_peru/).

## Brazil and Argentina: both sides of Iguazu rather than extreme sports

In Brazil, the usual sequence starts in Rio de Janeiro before continuing to [Foz do Iguacu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Paths in the Brazilian park provide broad views of the waterfalls. On the [Argentine side near Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), visitors walk closer to individual cascades and the Devil's Throat.

These are active walking excursions along maintained paths, **but not equivalent to mountain trekking or rafting**. Some programmes offer Macuco Safari as an additional paid excursion. Whether a boat trip is included must be checked against the specific tour conditions, not inferred from the word "Adventure".

The order of visits on the two sides affects logistics: travelling between parks involves an international border crossing. If a flight to Buenos Aires follows, the hours after the excursion cannot all be treated as free time. Ada Tours coordinates the sequence of stops and travel time so that sightseeing does not become a frantic rush to the airport.

## Chile: Atacama and preparation for the most demanding transfer

After Buenos Aires, many programmes continue to Santiago, then fly to Calama and travel overland to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). A key feature of this stage is **preparing to cross from Chile's dry desert into high-altitude Bolivia**.

San Pedro is surrounded by volcanic and desert scenery, but an overnight stay here does not in itself confirm participation in a demanding hike. Some programmes offer a separate evening astronomy excursion. It does not replace the main 4×4 journey and may cost extra.

As elevation increases, temperature, air humidity and the body's ability to cope with exertion change. Even travellers who easily managed the Iguazu walkways benefit from allowing time to acclimatise before reaching the plateau. When planning, discuss wellbeing, the number of overnight stops and the length of the overland section.

## Why a four-country page also requires a look at Bolivia

Around [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the relevant tours spend two busy days in 4×4 vehicles. Their programmes feature Laguna Verde, the Dali Desert, hot springs, a chain of high-altitude lagoons, the Chiguana Salt Flat and the salt expanses of Uyuni.

This stage differs markedly from an ordinary city excursion. Dirt roads, significant changes in elevation, long periods in a vehicle, cold morning stops and remote settlements call for preparation. **It is an expedition-style off-road section, not a guaranteed multi-day hiking trip.** Equipment and restrictions depend on the approved itinerary and included services.

If a 4×4 journey is your main goal, compare [adventure programmes through Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Peru](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_peru/interests/adventure/). Those programmes consider the same stops with the principal high-altitude stage in focus. Here, the important question is how that stage fits into a journey that also includes Argentina and Brazil's waterfalls.

## Peru: mountain roads, Cusco and Machu Picchu

From Bolivia, the route crosses the border towards [Puno and Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), then continues to Cusco by tourist bus. The journey includes stops at historic sites. An excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) follows.

Machu Picchu stands amid mountains, and visiting it requires time for the train, bus and a walk on an approved visitor circuit. However, **the usual included excursion to the citadel is not a trek on the Inca Trail**. A multi-day hike of that kind cannot be assumed unless explicitly listed.

The adventurous side of the Peruvian stage is therefore principally the dramatic change of scenery and a combination of high-altitude travel with archaeological walks. Anyone seeking a challenging trek should consider it as a separate product with its own requirements, not an automatically included part of these tours.

## Choosing a programme: from a busy trip to a major continental journey

The [18-day group tour through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) links Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago, Atacama, Uyuni and Cusco. It suits those seeking the contrast between humid lowlands and highlands who are comfortable with a relatively intensive schedule.

The [19-day Carnival programme](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) adds a festive evening in Rio, but does not automatically provide more time for the 4×4 section. The [20-day trip through six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) also includes sightseeing in Montevideo. This broadens the geography rather than adding an extreme-sports stage.

The [32-day tour through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues into Ecuador and Colombia. Its strength is broader geographical coverage, although much of the extra duration is also spent on flights, cities and new excursion programmes. It does not necessarily mean more days of hiking in each of the four countries.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_source_karnaval_5_stran,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## What to prepare before departure

For Brazil and Iguazu, pack lightweight clothing and rain protection; for Chile's desert and Bolivia's plateau, bring warm layers, protection from sun and wind, and comfortable footwear. Peru adds long journeys on mountain roads. Plan your luggage around the actual flights and the baggage allowances of the specific carriers.

First decide which activity matters most: waterfall walks, travelling by 4×4, archaeological routes or a longer mountain trek. We help match your priority to the days in existing programmes, check international crossings and allow reasonable recovery time after the high-altitude stages. Entry and border requirements are checked separately for the traveller's nationality.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in four countries

### Do these programmes include only Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Peru?

No. The adventure itineraries shown here also visit Bolivia, and some include additional countries. The filter names four selected principal countries but does not limit the full route to them.

### Will we trek the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu?

These programmes schedule a standard visit to Machu Picchu. A multi-day Inca Trail trek is not listed and must not be considered included.

### How do Iguazu walks differ from the 4×4 tour in the Andes?

Iguazu features walkways and viewpoints in humid forest. The Andean off-road section travels at high altitude along remote dirt roads and calls for different preparations.

### Can I remove Bolivia and keep the four countries?

That would change the actual programme and remove its principal off-road stage. A new itinerary would have to be agreed separately, together with a reassessment of what remains of the adventure theme.

### What matters more when choosing: the total number of days or days of activity?

Days devoted to the activities themselves. Extra time on a longer tour may be spent on flights, capitals and cultural excursions. Compare the day-by-day itinerary and the services included.

## Four countries and their cultures: what connects the itinerary

[Argentina](/argentina/), [Brazil](/brazil/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Peru](/peru/) make an appealing combination because one journey reveals **different historical traditions**, rather than four similar capitals. Rio de Janeiro illustrates how a Brazilian city developed between mountains and sea. Buenos Aires introduces the culture of the Rio de la Plata and tango. Santiago, Valparaiso and Chile's coastal districts reveal another kind of urban life. In Peru, the main historical thread leads into the Sacred Valley and Inca heritage.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which all four countries are on the principal itinerary and culture and history have a substantial role. However, **not every tour is limited to these four countries**. Some include Bolivia with Tiwanaku and Lake Titicaca, and the longest itineraries visit further South American countries. Compare [all tours for this country combination](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile_peru/) and [multi-country cultural journeys](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) to distinguish the geographical selection from the theme.

## Brazil: Rio as a cultural landscape

The cultural part of these itineraries usually begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Programmes include Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and city excursions. The [15-day Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) allocates several days to Rio before the flight to Iguazu.

UNESCO lists Rio as a cultural landscape shaped by the interaction between the city, the mountains and the sea. On such an itinerary, Corcovado and the views of the bay help explain how the terrain influenced the city's layout, architecture and public spaces. Walking through Rio's streets also matters to the historical story, not only climbing to its famous viewpoints.

When choosing a Carnival programme, check the specific event. On the [18-day journey with Rio's Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/), the parade is an explicit part of the itinerary. The usual [five-country group tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) does not list a Carnival event as a compulsory day. Similar geography does not mean an identical cultural programme.

## Argentina: Buenos Aires and tango as a living tradition

The next cultural stop is [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). After Iguazu Falls, the programmes include city sightseeing, and several longer itineraries feature a tango show. This is a very different urban story: Buenos Aires' neighbourhoods and squares, architecture, café culture and the music that emerged in the Rio de la Plata region.

UNESCO recognises tango as intangible cultural heritage shared by Argentina and Uruguay. This helps travellers understand why a performance is connected to the city's history, migration and everyday traditions, rather than simply being a random evening entertainment.

**Check whether the tango show is included in your selected programme.** For example, the [18-day group journey through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) includes a tango evening in the itinerary. The 15-day option has a city day and free time, but other activities need to be checked against its particular terms. The arrival date after the Argentine side of Iguazu also affects time in Buenos Aires: a border crossing and flight can take up much of a day.

## Chile: Santiago, Valparaiso and the transition to the Andes

[Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) connects the Argentine and Peruvian sections on the four-country route. The [15-day programme](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) includes an excursion from the capital to Viña del Mar and Valparaiso. Travellers can compare Santiago's business centre with Pacific coastal cities, hillside buildings, port history and seaside neighbourhoods.

On longer programmes, the Chilean section changes. After Santiago, travellers fly to Calama and continue to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The desert helps illustrate life in northern Chile and routes across the Andes, but days here are often focused on natural landscapes and preparing for the high-altitude stage. **A visit to Atacama should not be called a full historical or archaeological excursion unless a particular site appears in the itinerary.**

Choosing between Valparaiso and Atacama changes the entire pace of the journey. The first offers more time for coastal cities and culture. The second opens the way into Bolivia and high-altitude itineraries, adding flights, off-road travel and changing climates. These are different experiences, and a short tour should not promise both sets of sights without the corresponding days.

## Peru: the Sacred Valley, Cusco and Machu Picchu

Peru forms the principal archaeological section of the [15-day four-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/). The programme visits the Sacred Valley, Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Chinchero, Moray and Awanacancha, before taking the train towards [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Next come [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).

Machu Picchu is a monument of Inca civilisation in a mountain setting. It must not be confused with sites from other historical periods. Travelling through the valley and Cusco helps explain the network of settlements, terraces and roads, while Lima represents a different historical era and urban context.

Longer five- and six-country programmes add Puno, Lake Titicaca and the Uros Islands to this Peruvian section. In some, the Bolivian [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) comes before the border crossing and belongs to a different pre-Columbian culture from the Incas. This is particularly valuable for historical comparison, but **Bolivia is an additional country relative to the four named here**. Tiwanaku is not listed on the 15-day four-country itinerary.

Agree on a specific date and available visitor circuit for Machu Picchu in advance. Admission tickets and visiting procedures are regulated by the relevant Peruvian authorities and may change; an outdated excursion description does not replace confirmation of access for the day required.

## How the programmes differ culturally

| Itinerary | Principal distinction |
|---|---|
| [15 days, four countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) | Rio, Buenos Aires, Chilean cities, Inca Valley |
| [18 days, five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) | Atacama, Bolivia, Tiwanaku and Titicaca added |
| [18 days with the Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) | Rio event plus longer itinerary |
| [20 days, six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Uruguayan section also included |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_braziliya_argentina_chili_peru_ru,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_i_parad_chempionov_karnavala,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026}}

Dates, formats and included services vary between trips. Even two itineraries with similar titles may differ by a particular festive evening, the number of nights in a city or where the high-altitude section begins. To choose for cultural reasons, compare **the time available at each cultural site rather than the number of countries**.

## A historical itinerary needs time for transfers

Connecting Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago and Cusco generally requires several flights. A day of international travel seldom allows as much time for museums, old neighbourhoods and guided visits as a full day without changing cities. The Santiago–Cusco connection is especially important: in addition to flying, the traveller enters a different altitude, climate and pace.

On a multi-country journey, Ada Tours helps coordinate the sequence of cultural stops, flights, overland transfers and visiting time. Visa and transit requirements are checked separately according to nationality before booking, as are document validity, rules for domestic flights and payment conditions in each country. A Russian-issued or other foreign bank card should not be assumed to work as a universal payment method at every destination.

A trip from humid Rio to high-altitude Cusco calls for clothing suitable for varied temperatures and rainfall. The fewer days available, the more important it may be to drop a secondary stop in favour of a complete excursion to Machu Picchu or a chosen city's historic centre. The overall experience of the four countries depends on how well the time is distributed.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural travel in Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Peru

### Is there an itinerary covering exactly four countries without Bolivia?

Yes. The [15-day tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) visits Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru. Other programmes in this selection may add Bolivia, Uruguay and further countries.

### Which is more interesting for culture: Valparaiso or Atacama?

If Chilean urban history is the aim, the four-country tour includes Valparaiso and Viña del Mar. Atacama on longer itineraries primarily offers natural geography and high-altitude experiences, although it may form part of a broader historical journey.

### Is a tango show included on every tour visiting Buenos Aires?

No. Whether it is included and paid for depends on the specific programme. For example, the [18-day group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) lists a tango show among its days.

### Can I see both Machu Picchu and Tiwanaku on one journey?

Yes, but you need an itinerary through Bolivia and Peru. For example, the [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) includes both stops; the 15-day four-country tour does not include Tiwanaku.

### Does Machu Picchu need a dedicated day?

On current itineraries, the visit takes up a substantial part of a day and involves rail and overland travel. Confirm the tickets, visitor circuit and entry time before finalising flights and hotels.

## Why Rio's calendar determines the journey

For a combination of [Argentina](/argentina/), [Brazil](/brazil/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Peru](/peru/), we offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Every programme has a fifth principal country: [Bolivia](/bolivia/). This is a selection of itineraries intersecting in the four named countries, not a promise of a separate tour restricted to them.

The centre of the celebrations is [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The trip then becomes an extensive journey through South America: Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires neighbourhoods, Chilean desert and mountains, a Bolivian 4×4 route and the Inca heritage of Peru. Removing Rio would eliminate the advertised festive element; removing Bolivia would require the route between Atacama and Peru to be redesigned.

## Two festive programmes: New Year and Carnival

### New Year on Copacabana

On the [19-day New Year itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/), travellers arrive in Rio on 30 December. A visit to Christ the Redeemer and an evening on Copacabana are scheduled for 31 December, with Sugarloaf Mountain on 1 January. The day of 2 January is free, allowing time to rest after the late celebration before the longer journey begins.

A beach celebration and a private dinner in a hotel are different arrangements. Dinner or a party at a hotel on the beachfront is considered a separate booking option. Its cost and availability need to be agreed specifically.

### Rio Carnival and the Champions' Parade

On the [group trip with the Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/), the parade is scheduled for Day 2, after exploring Rio and Sugarloaf Mountain. The [private five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) sets aside a separate Carnival evening with a transfer to the Sambadrome. Travellers interested in a particular samba school or type of parade should compare these events rather than search for a generic "Carnival ticket."

According to LIESA's **2027 calendar**, performances by the top-tier samba schools are scheduled for 7, 8 and 9 February, and the **Champions' Parade for 13 February**. These are different dates and programmes. When choosing a departure, compare the night-time show, ticket type, Sambadrome sector and the following morning's transfer. Ready-made itineraries should not automatically be moved to another Carnival date.

## Five countries on the actual itinerary

| Stage | What is scheduled |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Rio, festive night, [Foz do Iguacu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) |
| Argentina | [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and tango |
| Chile | [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) |
| Bolivia | High-altitude lagoons, [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) |
| Peru | Lake Titicaca, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) |

The Argentine tango show is a cultural stop, **not an additional festival** within these offers. No separate festive events are listed in the Chilean, Bolivian or Peruvian sections either. They are important for a different reason: after the crowds and the ocean coast, travellers encounter a gradually changing landscape, from the Atacama Desert to high-altitude salt flats and Inca monuments.

In Santiago, the programme includes a city tour, while a separate wine excursion to the Maipo Valley and an astronomy outing in Atacama are among the excursion possibilities on the relevant routes. To determine exactly what is included in the price, distinguish standard days from optional activities: their presence in a description does not always mean the same conditions apply across every tour format.

## Flights, borders and changing altitude

Over 18–19 days, both climate and altitude change. Rio can be hot and humid during the day; Atacama is dry, while nights in high-altitude areas are much colder. The Bolivian section crosses lagoons and the salt flat in 4×4 vehicles before heading to La Paz and the Peruvian side of Titicaca. Travel time here cannot be assessed by measuring straight lines on a map.

Before paying, check three things: whether there is enough rest after the night at the Sambadrome, how the ascents to altitude are distributed and how much time is left for connections. Anyone sensitive to altitude should discuss the journey with a doctor in advance. Pack light clothes for the Atlantic coast, sun protection and warm layers for the Andes; baggage restrictions on domestic flights depend on the actual tickets.

Nationality determines which documents a participant needs for entry and transit through each of the five countries. Ada Tours can help structure the checks and plan the sequence of transfers, but an event date does not remove visa and border formalities.

## Which options to compare

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_i_parad_chempionov_karnavala,tour_source_karnaval_5_stran,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_na_16_dnej_na_novyj_god}}

The main choice is between a New Year tour with a celebration on 31 December and a Carnival departure; the next considerations are group or private travel, duration and included services. Compare not only price, but the number of nights in Rio before the long flights, time on both sides of Iguazu and the terms of the Sambadrome visit.

Other options can be found in the [general tours for these four countries](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile_peru/) and [multi-country events and festivals journeys](/multi-country/interests/events-and-festivals/). If the festival date is already fixed, choose the event first and then the programme that fits it.

## Frequently asked questions about festive tours through Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Peru

### Does this selection really include only four countries?

No. Every ready-made offer has a fifth country, Bolivia. The route from Atacama to Titicaca passes through it, so the filter must not be interpreted as a promise of a four-country trip without Bolivia.

### Is a Sambadrome ticket included in every tour?

That depends on the specific Carnival programme. The New Year itinerary concerns a different celebration. For Carnival, check the date and type of parade rather than transfer the conditions of one trip to another.

### Can I see Carnival and spend several days at Machu Picchu?

The itineraries combine Carnival in Rio with a Peruvian section visiting [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), but the length of the stop and entry time at the archaeological site are set by the programme. A longer stay in Peru would need a separately agreed itinerary change.

## What the culinary itinerary actually includes

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: the [20-day tour through six Latin American countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). In addition to Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Peru, it visits Uruguay and Bolivia. **This is an extensive sightseeing journey with some culinary experiences**, rather than a continuous tasting tour restricted to the four countries named in the title.

The main question is what has already been arranged and included, and what requires a separate booking. Hotel breakfasts or lunches on the road do not by themselves replace a substantial excursion about local cuisine. The [general four-country combination](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile_peru/) includes other itinerary options; here we focus on the culinary experiences of this particular tour.

## Argentina: a tango show with dinner

After the Argentine side of Iguazu, you arrive in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). The day's sightseeing takes in historic neighbourhoods including San Telmo, La Boca and Recoleta. In the evening, a [tango show with dinner](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-with-dinner/) is scheduled. The standalone excursion description mentions traditional dishes and Argentine wines.

This is a specific **included culinary event** connected to the city's culture. However, there is no separate wine trip to Mendoza, estate visit or series of tastings during the Argentine section. Anyone seeking an in-depth introduction to Argentine winemaking would need to change the geography and timing of the journey separately.

The following day is devoted to a ferry trip to Montevideo in Uruguay. Free time there is not equivalent to a prearranged culinary tour.

## Chile: the Maipo Valley at additional cost

In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a sightseeing tour of the city centre is included. During that stage, it is **also possible to book** a [Maipo Valley wine tour](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/) with a tasting. The current programme specifies a separate price and a minimum number of participants: this option **is not included in the basic services**.

The [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) is known for vineyards and Cabernet Sauvignon. A relaxed winery visit needs its own block of time for transfers, the tour and tasting. After Santiago, the itinerary continues towards Calama and San Pedro de Atacama, so the wine programme cannot simply be moved to the next day without revising the schedule.

If the wine experience matters more than some of the general sightseeing stops, an additional night near Santiago may be worth discussing. The specific winery and tasting selection must be agreed separately; the current tour does not name them.

## Brazil: Rio and Iguazu without a food excursion

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), you visit Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and city neighbourhoods, before travelling to [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). This is a busy cultural and natural itinerary, but **it does not include a cooking class, food-market tour or cachaça tasting**.

Brazilian food traditions can be explored independently, but being in a city does not mean a culinary service is included. For a different specialisation, compare [food and wine tours in Brazil](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/brazil/).

## Peru: from Titicaca to Lima, without a promised culinary tour

The Peruvian days pass through Lake Titicaca, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). Some days include lunch, but the programme focuses on transfers, archaeological sites and city sightseeing. A fine-dining restaurant visit, guided food-market outing or cooking lesson is not listed in the approved conditions.

Peru has a rich culinary tradition, but specific tastings cannot be expected without time set aside for them. If exploring Lima's food is your goal, additional stops would need to be agreed without cutting necessary flights and transfers to essential sights.

## Who the programme suits

The [extended 20-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) suits travellers whose main goal is to see Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago, Uyuni and Machu Picchu, with culinary experiences along the way. **A tango evening with dinner is included; Maipo is a separate add-on.** A full wine or food-focused trip across the four countries would require further stops and time.

After Chile, the programme continues through the highlands of Bolivia and Peru. Tastings must be planned around transfers, altitude and wellbeing. For specialised alternatives, start with [Food and Wine](/interests/food-and-wine/) and [multi-country culinary tours](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the Maipo tasting included?

No. Maipo Valley winery visits are offered at an extra charge, with a minimum participant requirement.

### Is there an Argentine culinary evening?

Yes. Buenos Aires includes a tango show with dinner and local dishes.

### Is there a dedicated culinary excursion in Peru?

Not on the current itinerary. The Peruvian days are mainly devoted to the monuments of Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima.

## Four countries with very different nature experiences

[Brazil](/brazil/) and [Argentina](/argentina/) share one of the continent's most recognisable natural landmarks: Iguazu Falls. [Peru](/peru/) offers mountain valleys and the scenery around [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). In [Chile](/chile/), nature experiences depend on the programme: the shorter option includes Santiago and the coast, while longer itineraries continue to Atacama.

Our themed selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with all four countries forming part of the principal geography. Some tours add Bolivia, Uruguay, Ecuador or Colombia. The same list of countries in a filter therefore **does not mean identical nature excursions**.

| Format | Main highlights |
|---|---|
| 4 countries, 15 days | Iguazu, Peru's mountains |
| 5 countries, 18–19 days | Atacama, lagoons, Uyuni |
| 6–8 countries | Extension into other regions |

The [general multi-country nature catalogue](/multi-country/interests/nature/) offers other combinations. Here the aim is to understand how current trips through Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Peru differ.

## Iguazu: two natural parks on opposite sides of a border

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), you will see granite cliffs, Corcovado's forested slopes and Sugarloaf Mountain above the bay. Travellers then continue to [Foz do Iguacu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), where the Brazilian side provides a sweeping view of the waterfalls.

The Argentine section of the complex lies near [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). A different network of walkways and viewpoints brings visitors closer to individual cascades. UNESCO recognises the natural significance of Argentina's Iguazu National Park and its surrounding forest. For travellers, the important point is that **these are two distinct visits** separated by border control.

On the [15-day four-country tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/), a separate day is devoted to the Brazilian side, while the Argentine side is combined with a flight to Buenos Aires. Read the schedule carefully: how many hours remain for the trails, which airport the flight uses and how much time is allowed at the border. Some areas may temporarily close after heavy rainfall.

## Chile: the Pacific coast or the Atacama Desert

On the 15-day itinerary, the Chilean stage visits [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [Valparaiso with Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). Travellers can see the Andes around the capital and the Pacific coast. However, **this itinerary does not include a separate excursion to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/)**.

On the [18-day journey through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), the route continues after Santiago through Calama to San Pedro, before entering Bolivia's high-altitude section. Desert landscapes, volcanic terrain, coloured lagoons and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) then come into the itinerary.

The choice is quite different. If Atacama attracts you, do not regard it as a short evening outing from Santiago: it calls for a flight, overland transportation, extra days and preparation for altitude. Choose a programme that already includes northern Chile on the main route.

## Peru: the Sacred Valley and mountain roads

In Peru, natural scenery stands alongside archaeology. The [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) is surrounded by Andean slopes, while the route to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) crosses mountainous terrain. The compact 15-day itinerary allows several consecutive days in this region.

However, a visit to Machu Picchu **is not the same as a multi-day mountain hike**. Sightseeing may involve climbing steps and walking on uneven paths, but a dedicated trek must be explicitly included in the programme. Admission tickets and visitor circuits have specific restrictions that matter when booking.

[Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) lies at roughly 3,350 metres above sea level. Even fit travellers may experience altitude symptoms after a rapid flight from the lowlands. The CDC Yellow Book advises planning acclimatisation and considering the elevation of overnight stops. Individual medical risks and preventive medication should be discussed with a doctor.

## 15, 18, 20 or 32 days: comparing nature-focused journeys

If your main goals are Iguazu and the Andean scenery of Peru, the [15-day four-country tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) is a suitable option. It combines natural attractions with a substantial urban and cultural programme.

The [18-day group journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) adds Bolivia, Atacama, high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni. The [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) also visits Uruguay. The [32-day extended itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) goes further into Ecuador, the Galapagos Islands and Colombia.

A longer trip does not necessarily mean more time **specifically at Iguazu or in the Sacred Valley**: added days may be spent on flights, cities and new countries. Compare the actual nature excursions and their physical demands day by day rather than simply looking at total duration.

Our selection also includes a [private Carnival itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) and a [New Year journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/). They differ chiefly in the festive context at the start; their nature stops should be checked separately.

## Climate, altitude and luggage for four countries

Rio and Iguazu are often hot and humid. Chile's coast can have a cool wind, while Cusco and Peru's mountain regions are markedly colder after sunset. Programmes including Bolivia add cold nights on the high plateau and strong daytime sunlight. There is no single "perfect month for all of South America".

Pack lightweight clothing for hot regions, rain protection for the waterfalls, warm clothes for the Andes, comfortable shoes and UV protection. Check baggage allowances before booking domestic flights, especially when different airlines operate the segments.

Entry requirements must be checked **for every country actually visited**, considering nationality, passport, transit and the manner of crossing each border. Ada Tours helps coordinate transfers, connections and visits to natural attractions, without promising decisions on behalf of immigration authorities or park administrations.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Peru

### Is Atacama included on every tour in this selection?

No. The [15-day programme](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) visits Santiago and the coast. To see Atacama, choose an itinerary with San Pedro and the high-altitude section, usually including Bolivia.

### Why visit Iguazu from both sides?

The Brazilian and Argentine parks offer different views and walking routes. Both visits require attention to border crossings and schedules, especially when a flight is planned for the same day.

### Which is more physically demanding: Machu Picchu or Uyuni?

In Peru, walking, steps and Cusco's altitude matter. Travelling from Atacama to Uyuni adds many hours in 4×4 vehicles and overnight stays at high altitude. The choice depends on health, pace and the sequence of overnight stops.
